newsitem.title: ISRAEL: No survivors in Israeli helicopter crash.
newsitem.headline: No survivors in Israeli helicopter crash.

text.p: Hospitals prepared to receive a flood of wounded soldiers from the worst air force disaster in Israeli history.
Rescue workers pulled bodies and body parts from the wreckage of the crash in northern Israel -- but no survivors.
The army placed the death toll at close to 70 soldiers.
Twisted metal was strewn over a one-kilometre radius in the farming community of Shaar Yishuv. The helicopters were taking commanders and fighters to Lebanon.
"We heard people yelling but it was soft, probably the last gasps of people who had been wounded," said Dalia Golan, one of the first residents to arrive at the crash site.
"I tried to find a pulse on one of them but to my sorrow there was no pulse," she said.
The U.S.-made Sikorsky helicopters were taking soldiers to Israel's self-declared south Lebanon occupation zone in stormy weather. The aircraft collided moments after liftoff.
"I ran outside and saw a ball of fire descending. We didn't know exactly where but by instinct my husband ran to the car and I took my medical bag because I'm a nurse," Golan said.
One of the helicopters crashed into a bungalow, setting it ablaze.
Large pieces of aircraft were recovered in marshy farmland where soldiers waded through mud to reach the wreckage.
The propeller of one helicopter slammed into a road, leaving a gash in the pavement.
Security officials said the helicopters were packed with ammunition. Rescue workers were careful not to set off explosions during the futile search for survivors.
Army spokesman Oded Ben-Ami said the cause was under investigation. He ruled out a guerrilla attack.
Witnesses said soldiers were stacking bodies at concentration points before taking them to a local army base for identification.
"I saw about 30 bodies on the ground. Some had their legs cut off...They were all lined up on the side of the road," a witness said.
